summary_paragraph: A man with a history of ischemic cardiomyopathy, atrial fibrillation, coronary stents, COPD, and polysubstance use was admitted for chest pain and dyspnea on exertion. He had been noncompliant with all medications, including anticoagulants and diuretics, for two months. Evaluation revealed acute on chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (LVEF 30%), elevated proBNP, and fluid overload, but no acute coronary syndrome. A pharmacologic stress test showed fixed perfusion defects with no reversible ischemia. He was treated with IV diuresis, restarted on guideline-directed heart failure medications, and had his lisinopril dose increased. His symptoms improved, and he was discharged home with plans to follow up on medication reconciliation, lab monitoring, and mental health support.
